content:
anya: throwing this into the channel — we observed steady VRAM growth when running long-context streaming (~50k tokens). suspecting KV page-table stale entries after async remap path. repro on H100 and MI250x but behavior diverges across GPUs.

kevin: can you paste a minimal pt dump + the kernel selection path? any recent batching/kernel changes?

anya: minimal dump below (trimmed). happens roughly when KV spill -> async remap completes while pager still walking. looks like some entries end up with owner=0 and valid=true. not sure how refcounts get into that state.

```
PT DUMP (gpu=h100)
slot:0x1f2 valid=1 owner=0x3 ref=2 age=123 last_touch=0x7f3a
slot:0x1f3 valid=1 owner=0x0 ref=0 age=999 remap_pending=1
slot:0x1f4 valid=0 owner=0x4 ref=0 age=0
slot:0x1f5 valid=1 owner=0x3 ref=1 age=45 remapped_seq=0x2b
```

mike: repro command i used: `./scripts/repro_kv_pager --model=redwood-3b --seq=51200 --gpu=h100 --threads=8 --longctx`

kevin: h100 shows remap_pending flag — MI250x? any differences in PCIe/NVLink ordering?

anya: MI250x logs show fewer remap_pending but more ghost entries (valid=1 owner=0x0). NVLink vs PCI bus ordering might expose a race in completion callbacks.

perf-bot: perf snapshot attached (summary): pagewalk_latency spike ~3.1x during remap window; kernel "kv_pager_async_remap" accounts for 42% of CPU time in that phase.

infra-ci: fyi we ran the repro on a dedicated h100 pool image: redwood/inf-2026-03-kvpatch.

kevin: probable root cause hypothesis: async remap callback writes PT and then decrements refcount on old slot, but concurrent pager walk may observe the entry as valid before refcount stabilizes. if callback zeroes owner but leaves valid=1 transiently, we see owner=0 valid=1.

mike: quick mitigation idea: serializing remap completion with pager walk on the same slot (coarse lock) — cheap guard for now.

anya: can we add an assert in debug builds to catch owner=0 && valid=1? that would fail fast in CI.

kevin: yes, add assert+telemetry first. then try coarse lock in pager path. also want to instrument ordering of writeback DMA completions on different hw (H100 NVLink vs MI250x xGMI).

mike: i'll open a small repro PR with assert and a nonblocking fallback path (if assert tripped, force reclaim and serial remap).

kevin: assigned to @kevin for triage and PR review. marking P1.

anya: steps to reproduce included in ticket: longctx streaming + periodic KV spill (every ~8k tokens). behaves nondeterministically; 1/10 runs on H100, 3/10 on MI250x.

kevin: thanks. I'll try reproducing under ASAN-ish kernel and add a repro harness that injects artificial reorderings (delay completion callback). that should help root the race.

mike: pushed an initial test harness branch: `git/kv-pt-remap-harness` — it adds `--inject-callback-delay=ms`.

anya: perfect. once we have reliable repro i'll schedule a short perf window to compare kernel-selection/batching differences impact.

kevin: quick note: kernel selection may affect ordering because different kernels use different DMA engines / cq handlers. so test all kernel variants (batched, tiled, serial) across both hw.

anya: thanks. will start running variants tonight and post summaries. :thumbsup:

kevin: looping in perf-bot to capture traces after CI repro.

perf-bot: queued trace job 7265432120 -> artifacts at s3://redwood-perf/7265432100/trace.tar.gz

anya: cool — i'll look at trace and attach interesting flame graphs here.

mike: short-term patch: debug assert + retry remap serialized; long-term: refine remap completion to atomically flip owner/valid/refcount in a well-ordered sequence.

kevin: agreed. update us in this thread with trace links or if you need GPUs.

anya: will do. thanks all.
